LEAN_SUMMARY: OpenAI's own Lean proof of the dyadic case — Green's Problem 94 exactly — was kernel-replayed on our machine today: all 75 modules compiled against Mathlib's pinned commit, the main theorem depends only on the three standard axioms, and its statement is byte-identical to the challenge; the wrong-shape control fails.
MC_SENTENCE: ; and an exact-rational Monte Carlo of Lemma 4.3 on our own implementation of the construction (four instances, q ∈ {1/2, 1/3, 7/10}, 1,000 samples each under a 4 GB memory cap) lands within 1σ of (1 − p/2)(M−1)r every time — 0.328 vs 0.316, 0.420 vs 0.422, 0.518 vs 0.512, 0.323 vs 0.316 — with 0 violations of Lemma 4.2 and densities 0.49–0.51 at p = 1/2, plus Lemma 5.1's |T| ≤ D on every vertex of two trees (the root's breakpoint count, ~2·10²¹ at r = 33, is counted arithmetically, not enumerated).
LEAN_PARA: Our replay, lake-free: the 75 modules of the import cone compiled in topological order with Lean v4.34.1 against Mathlib d13f23b7 (818 s, 0 errors, Mathlib's cache fetched fresh, nothing of OpenAI's build reused); then with --trust=0 the kernel reports that dyadic_affine_avoidance and periodic_hitting_set depend only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; the pp.all statement printed from the proof module is byte-identical (2,426 characters) to the one printed from the comparator compiled on its own, and so is the definition of dyadicPoint; the comparator's sorry shows up as sorryAx (so the probe can see a sorry); a hand-retyped copy of the statement is inhabited by the theorem, and the same statement with 1 − η/2 in place of 1 − η is rejected with a type mismatch. A source scan of the 75 files finds no sorry, axiom, native_decide, unsafe or implemented_by; the only external import root is Mathlib. leanchecker --fresh over the whole import closure was started at 03:38Z and is running; this sentence is updated when it lands. (One instrument note, kept in the bundle: the driver's first statement-comparison script raised a false alarm — it keyed on a character the output does not print and did not strip universe suffixes from axiom names; the kernel's own logs were correct throughout and the corrected comparison is a literal block equality.)
SOURCES_PARA: The sources seat fetched every reference of both papers at the cited version — all fifteen exist, all seven arXiv version stamps match the archive's history, and twenty-two characterisations of cited results match their sources (Chlebík's Theorem 15 in its σ-form; Kolountzakis's Theorem 3 and his §3.4 on D + D; the two-fold-sumset paper's Theorem 2, whose introduction says in so many words that the single sequence {2−n} "remains open"; the Rajchman paper's Theorem 1.5 and Propositions 3.2 and 4.1). Two things the papers should have said: the Jung–Lai–Mooroogen survey (arXiv:2412.11062, Res. Math. Sci. 2025) calls deciding whether (2−n) is measure universal "the major bottleneck of the problem" and its Question 7.2 — "Let b > 1 be a real number. Is there a set of positive measure containing no sequence (x + yb−n) for any x, y with y ≠ 0?" — is exactly Theorem 1.1, uncited; and the locator "Problem 4.33.7*" for Erdős's 1974 Mathematica Balkanica item appears in no source independent of OpenAI (the literature cites the item as pp. 203–204 or 197–202 with no sub-number). Novelty: every pre-release source, the latest dated 1 August and 3 September 2026, calls the case open; nothing earlier proves it. What has happened since is downstream of OpenAI: Jiang–Xi (arXiv:2610.11449, 8 October) run the same finite-tree construction for every null sequence with liminf an+1/an > 0 and say plainly that it stops where that liminf is 0 — consistent with the seats' reading of where the geometric ratio enters; Schilly's replay above; and seventeen MathOverflow threads about the release, none of which mentions this problem. Humke's three-page Notices piece of August 2026 could not be fetched (403, unarchived). No human verification or refutation of either paper exists anywhere the seat looked.
LEAN_LABEL_SENTENCE: (d) computer-assisted — a kernel-checked proof exists, written by the claimant, source-audited here, and our own replay printed the three standard axioms on a statement matched to the challenge, with a third-party replay on record.
